pages.text: Everything that lives carries a clock. It also carries a weight, a haste, a size and a mind.$(br2)These are not organs. They are $(l)attributes$(), and they can be drawn out of a creature like blood. I call them the $(l)aspects$(), and measure them in $(l)drams$().

pages.title: What Happens to Them
pages.text: $(l)Density$(): drained, a creature floats. Drain more, it rises. Only a $(item)leash$() holds it down.$(br)$(l)Speed$(): it slows, then stands rooted.$(br)$(l)Size$(): it shrinks.$(br)$(l)Awareness$(): it thinks less often, then not at all.$(br)$(l)Time$(): it ages, then crumbles to dust.

pages.title: It Does Not Come Back
pages.text: A drained cow stays drained. To keep experimenting I must $(l)breed$() them: calves are born full.$(br2)Awareness evaporated before I could stopper the vial. Glass will not hold it. I need something that can hold more. Something that $(o)wants$() it.
